what: The CRATE-LEVEL interning ids this body's aggregate types carry, keyed by canonical FIRST-USE index.
why: THE CALLER for the 2026-09-16 tuple image. `IRTy.tuple_` existed in the object language but `a2project` had no image for `trust_ir::Ty::Tuple`, so no chain could carry one; this body spells `(usize, enum.33)` in three instructions and cannot be projected without it. It is also the body that makes the aggregate-construction gap CONCRETE: it is six instructions from a body of TypeChecker::infer_type's derived closure, and the machine halts inside it.
how_it_is_used: `ir_mint::mint` reads the enums lane to mint the type alias; `project` reads the interface block and refuses a fixture whose header or parameters are not the pinned ones.
interface_what: The artifact facts the CORE MODULE cannot hold and the emitted text does print.
interface_producer_invariance: `ty` is CANONICAL; `observed_ty` is verbatim, RECORDED and NEVER COMPARED.
tuple_what: ONE tuple type, `(usize, enum.33)` -- the `Iterator::size_hint` return pair. `IRTy.tuple_` takes a Nat and the reflected module has no tuple table to index, so the image is ARITY-ONLY: `(tuple 2)`, with the element types ERASED. A body differing only by `(ptr, enum.33)` would project to the SAME core. `tuple_sites` below is what makes that visible, exactly as ir_ni's `usize.sites` catches a u64-for-usize swap the resolved core cannot. Arity-only is enough for the machine: insertfield and extractfield ignore the declared type and work structurally over the value's spine.

usize.target_fact: aarch64-apple-darwin, a 64-bit target. Reader A resolved with --usize-bits 64 and recorded usize_sites_resolved: 1 -- the `const usize 0` that becomes the lower bound of the size hint.
usize.erasure_note: The resolved core spells the site as the plain (uint 64), so a u64-for-usize swap is caught by the count above and not by the core text.
